- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends or after prolonged high values.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after a spike, then gradually corrects — suggest smoothing or dampening after peak.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model often holds high values longer than observed.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — delays correction by 1–3 periods.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when history includes recent highs — consider adjusting for recent mean.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum; reduce forecast volatility in low-activity periods.
